title: Dipke seeks exemption from appearance in ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest case in Delhi

ai.summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke requested exemption from court appearance in the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' protest case, claiming family commitments and illness. Police detained him during the October protest demanding Chief Election Commissioner resignation.

facts.claim: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke sought exemption from appearing before the Special Executive Magistrate, Mandir Marg
facts.quote: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke sought exemption from appearing before the Special Executive Magistrate, Mandir Marg, on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

facts.claim: The next hearing is scheduled for December 2
facts.quote: The next hearing is scheduled for December 2.

facts.claim: There was no specific order saying that he had to appear today before the magistrate
facts.quote: There was no specific order saying that he had to appear today before the magistrate.

facts.claim: We filed for an exemption anyway, as he had family commitments and was unwell
facts.quote: We filed for an exemption anyway, as he had family commitments and was unwell

facts.claim: Mr. Dipke was detained under BNSS Sections 126 and 170 during the October 16 'Lehra Do Tiranga' (wave the tricolour) protest at Connaught Place
facts.quote: Mr. Dipke was detained under BNSS Sections 126 and 170 during the October 16‘‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ (wave the tricolour) protest at Connaught Place

facts.claim: seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
facts.quote: seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar

ai.background_note: Dipke was detained during a protest demanding Chief Election Commissioner resignation; the protest is part of the anti-SIR movement which involves voter list rechecks by the Election Commission.
